note: Round 2: opposite of the fox scene. Loose splashed ink, mostly monochrome, one warm accent, subject left and text space right. Dragon painted like Chen Rong (public domain refs from Wikimedia Commons).
prompt: The attached images are details of Chen Rong's Nine Dragons handscroll (1244). Use them as the guide for how the dragon is painted: loose wet ink, the head, a claw and a few coils emerging from cloud and spray while the rest of the body dissolves into ink wash and mist; scales only suggested by a few dry-brush strokes. Do not copy their exact composition. Make a Chinese ink painting on pale aged rice paper in the bold, spontaneous splashed-ink style (pomo and xieyi): fast, wild, confident brushstrokes, ink splashes and wet washes bleeding into the paper, large areas of bright empty paper. Mostly black and grey ink, only a little pale blue-green on a few rocks, and exactly one small warm accent of colour. The dragon is painted with the same loose brushwork as the landscape, never detailed, never a modern fantasy illustration. Wide horizontal composition. The subject sits in the left half; the right third is calm, bright, empty misty paper, kept free for text. No seal stamps, no written characters, no calligraphy, no text, no signature, no border. Not a digital painting, no 3D, no photorealism.

runs.label: b-storm
runs.prompt: Scene: a storm over jagged peaks. Dark splashed-ink clouds and slanting rain whirl around; a dragon claws its way upward through the storm on the left, only its head, one claw and a few coils visible in the churning cloud, reaching toward a small pale red sun breaking through at the top. The red sun is the one warm accent.

runs.label: c-dragon-gate
runs.prompt: Scene: the Dragon Gate legend. A tall waterfall pours down a cliff on the left, painted in a few bold strokes of wet ink and white paper. At its foot, in the spray, a small orange carp leaps high up the falls; it is the one warm accent. Above the top of the falls, a dragon is forming out of the mist and spray, half cloud, only its head and a claw clear.
